author: BreitbartNews
title: Conservative Groups File FCC Petitions to Block ABC's Broadcast License Renewal
text:
Multiple conservative organizations have submitted formal petitions to the FCC urging denial of ABC's broadcast license renewal, citing systemic partisan bias, DEI-driven discrimination, equal time violations, and alleged collusion with Chinese interests. The challenge follows an FCC probe into ABC's practices initiated by Commissioner Brendan Carr. ABC denies the accusations as politically motivated.
A group of petitions filed by several conservative organizations are seeking to deny ABC's broadcast license renewal, accusing the Disney-owned network of a range of misconduct including sexual discrimination, political violence, violations of the FCC's equal time rule , and collusion with Chinese operatives.
The campaign has gained momentum after Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chief Brendan Carr announced an investigation into the network's policies and opened the renewal process to formal objections. Carr indicated the FCC is scrutinizing ABC's diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) initiatives as well as alleged equal time violations involving programs like Jimmy Kimmel's late-night show and the daytime talk show "The View.
" One leading petitioner, the Center for American Rights, argues that ABC has failed to operate "in the public interest" due to what it describes as a consistent and overt partisan bias. The group's filing claims the network disregards longstanding FCC precedents designed to protect news integrity, engages in explicit racial and gender discrimination, soft-pedals coverage of the Chinese government's human rights abuses, and otherwise breaches its public trust obligations.
The Center for American Rights asserts that these failings make ABC unworthy of a renewed license. Another petitioner, the non-profit media watchdog Media Research Center (MRC), is seeking to torpedo the renewal on multiple grounds, including what it calls "continued and sustained abuse" of broadcast licenses, efforts to improperly influence national elections, and willful promotion of misinformation and political violence.
The MRC's complaint extends to ABC's owned-and-operated stations, such as WABC in New York, which it accuses of using the public airwaves to suppress critical stories, engage in relentless partisan campaigning, excuse political violence, and disseminate defamatory content. The organization urges the FCC to deny the renewal outright, citing a demonstrated pattern of serious legal violations, or alternatively to impose stringent conditions to force compliance.
America First Legal, a conservative legal group, has also filed a petition, contending that ABC's stations lack the necessary character qualifications to hold broadcast licenses. FCC Chief Carr has not provided a specific timeline for adjudicating these petitions, noting that the process will proceed at the pace required to thoroughly apply the Communications Act and relevant commission rules. The outcome of these challenges could have significant implications for the network's broadcast operations, though cable and streaming platforms remain unaffected.
This coordinated effort reflects broader partisan tensions over media bias and regulatory oversight, with critics of ABC alleging a systemic liberal slant in its news and entertainment programming while the network maintains its commitment to editorial independence and public service journalism
